1	# WP-001: Credential and Repository Type Definitions
     2	
     3	## Plan Context
     4	
     5	Extend the Git credentials system from a single-token-per-host model to a multi-credential model with per-repository credential association, auto-selection for single-match hosts, and clear error surfacing for missing credentials.
     6	
     7	## Description
     8	
     9	Define the new `GitCredentialEntry` interface in the config types and add the optional `CredentialId` field to the `Repository` type. These are the foundational type changes that all downstream work packages depend on.
    10	
    11	## Scope
    12	
    13	- `src/config/config.types.ts` — new `GitCredentialEntry` interface, changed `AppConfig.gitCredentials` type
    14	- `src/models/repository/repository.types.ts` — new `CredentialId` optional field on `Repository`
    15	
    16	## Deliverables
    17	
    18	- `GitCredentialEntry` interface with `id`, `label`, `host`, and `token` string fields
    19	- `AppConfig.gitCredentials` type changed from `Record<string, string> | undefined` to `GitCredentialEntry[] | undefined`
    20	- `Repository` type extended with `CredentialId?: string` field
    21	
    22	## Dependencies
    23	
    24	- None
    25	
    26	## Acceptance Criteria
    27	
    28	1. `GitCredentialEntry` interface exists in `src/config/config.types.ts` with fields `id: string`, `label: string`, `host: string`, `token: string`.
    29	2. `AppConfig.gitCredentials` is typed as `GitCredentialEntry[] | undefined` (no longer `Record<string, string> | undefined`).
    30	3. `Repository` type in `src/models/repository/repository.types.ts` includes an optional `CredentialId?: string` field.
    31	4. The project compiles with `tsc --noEmit` without type errors (excluding errors in files that consume the old type signatures — those are addressed in downstream WPs).
    32	
    33	## Active Pipeline Stages
    34	
    35	`implementation` → `qa` → `code-review` → `documentation`
    36	
    37	## Estimated Complexity
    38	
    39	Low
    40	
    41	## Rationale
    42	
    43	The array-with-explicit-`id` format was chosen over a nested map (`Record<string, Array<{label, token}>>`) because arrays are simpler to index, reference from repositories via a single `id` field, and iterate in the GUI. A nested map would require compound keys (host + index) for repository references, which is fragile and harder to display. `CredentialId` lives on `Repository` (not Project or Workspace) because credentials are tied to the remote URL, which is a repository-level concern.
    44	
    45	## Rejected Approaches
    46	
    47	- `Record<string, Array<{label, token}>>` (host-keyed map of arrays) — would require composite keys for repository references and is harder to iterate in the GUI.
    48	- Credential stored inline on Repository — duplicates tokens across repositories using the same credential.
    49	- Credential resolved purely by host matching (no explicit reference) — breaks deterministic resolution when multiple credentials exist for the same host.
    50	
    51	## Notes
    52	
    53	This WP introduces type-level breaking changes. Code that references `AppConfig.gitCredentials` as a `Record` will fail to compile until updated in downstream WPs (config parsing, credential resolution, API routes, orchestrators). This is intentional — the type system enforces that all consumers are updated.
